sources.label: Chung et al. (2018)
sources.note: Correct identity for DESY record 400022. SESS in negative GVD before fission; does not establish a normal-dispersion bound.
sources.where: Publisher abstract reproduced in PubMed; DESY download returned an empty-text page.

sources.label: Eisenberg et al. (2024)
sources.note: Argon hollow-core SESS demonstration; supports an application, not a universal efficiency ceiling.

sources.label: Finot, Chaussard and Boscolo (2018)
sources.note: Corrects the author attribution 'Aston', which is an institution. Interference description predicts spectral patterns; no optimized band-fraction bound.
sources.where: arXiv PDF; introduction and spectral-pattern analysis.

sources.label: Finot et al. (2008)
sources.note: Wave-breaking contribution to normally dispersive continuum formation, including gain/loss. The abstract does not verify a universal saturation theorem.
sources.where: Publisher and University of Southampton abstract.

sources.label: Heidt (2010)
sources.note: Identifiable replacement for the vague Heidt reference: coherent pulse-preserving ANDi generation, not a band-energy ceiling.

sources.label: Castelló-Lurbe, Andrés and Silvestre (2013)
sources.note: Equations 2 and 19 give the same dispersion-weighted Hamiltonian invariant; normal-dispersion spectral design already uses it.
sources.where: Author-uploaded paper on ResearchGate; section 2 and appendix.

sources.label: Castelló-Lurbe, Vermeulen and Silvestre (2016)
sources.note: Generalized inverse dispersive and nonlinear lengths sum to a constant. A direct optical precedent for the proposed invariant-based analysis.
sources.where: Full paper PDF indexed by web; introduction, section 2 and references.

sources.label: Wang, Chen and Chang (2022)
sources.note: Sections 3–4 estimate SPM/GVD spectral peak positions and widths for Gaussian/sech launches using a fitted lumped-chirp parameter. These are approximate spectral-width maxima, not optimized band-energy ceilings.
sources.where: Author PDF https://in.iphy.ac.cn/upload/s20/m/202212081457426583.pdf, local wang2022.pdf; Sections 3–4 and Table 1 inspected. Publisher article also mirrored on ResearchGate.

sources.label: Diao, Chen and Chang (2021)
sources.note: PSO varies fiber length, mode-field diameter and dispersion for a fixed Gaussian input. The fitness combines both outer-lobe energy fractions with pulse Strehl quality; this is prior optimization, not a global one-band ceiling.
sources.where: Publisher full article mirrored on ResearchGate, DOI 10.1364/OE.442348; Section 3 and Eqs. 5–7 inspected: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/355934392_Particle_swarm_optimization_of_SPM-enabled_spectral_selection_to_achieve_an_octave-spanning_wavelength-shift

sources.label: Deift and Zhou (2003)
sources.note: Defocusing NLS long-time asymptotics in weighted Sobolev spaces are established, including a logarithmic phase. Rewriting them in optical units alone is not novel.

sources.label: Koch and Tataru (2018)
sources.note: Conserved energies control Sobolev norms. Higher invariants are nonlinear functionals, not conserved ordinary Fourier moments.

sources.label: Zheltikov (2018)
sources.note: Explicitly distinguishes the NLSE norm from physical photon number and explains the role of the optical shock term.
sources.where: APS accepted manuscript; introduction and field equations.

sources.label: Epstein (2004)
sources.note: NMR inverse-scattering trace formulas yield minimum RF pulse energy for a prescribed magnetization profile. Different observable, but close optimization precedent.
sources.where: ScienceDirect abstract and indexed author-copy abstract; full download failed.

sources.label: Kuzyk (2000)
sources.note: Quantum sum-rule limits constrain molecular third-order susceptibility; they do not solve fixed-material fiber propagation efficiency.

sources.label: Akhmediev and Karlsson (1995)
sources.note: Abstract explicitly promises an analytic amount of radiation, not phase matching alone; full quantitative scope remains to be checked.

sources.label: Elgin, Brabec and Kelly (1995)
sources.note: Associate-field inverse-scattering perturbation describes radiation growth and structure as well as soliton changes.

sources.label: Erkintalo et al. (2012)
sources.note: Cascaded phase matching and nonlinear symmetry breaking in fiber combs; supports the cascaded mixing mechanism.

sources.label: Webb et al. (2013)
sources.note: Generalized radiation from non-solitonic pulses; a soliton-tail-only yield argument needs a restricted input class.

sources.label: Roy, Bhadra and Agrawal (2009), PRA
sources.note: Equations 2 and 6 provide a TOD/soliton-order radiation-peak-power law. The reported saturation concerns peak power, not integrated photon yield.
sources.where: Author-copy PDF via web index; sections II–V; direct download was unavailable.

sources.label: Roy, Bhadra and Agrawal (2009), OL
sources.note: Higher dispersion orders change the number and location of radiation peaks; no universal integrated-yield statement in the abstract.

sources.label: Roy et al. (2010)
sources.note: Dispersion-profile effects on radiation emission; a direct precursor that must be read fully before claiming an optimized law.
sources.where: ScienceDirect search-indexed abstract; author PDF located, not fetched.

sources.label: Webb et al. (2014)
sources.note: Effective soliton order, compression and finite fiber length explain efficiency trends for a dual-frequency beat input.

sources.label: Austin et al. (2006)
sources.note: Compression-window emission and recoil-induced blue shift are already identified; they are not missing mechanisms.

sources.label: Chang, Chen and Kärtner (2010)
sources.note: Efficient visible Cherenkov conversion is a source demonstration; its energy efficiency is not Roy's peak-power observable.

sources.label: Chang, Chen and Kärtner (2011)
sources.note: Few-cycle Cherenkov conversion study; broadband/shock physics limits comparison with the narrowband TOD model.

sources.label: Modotto et al. (2015)
sources.note: Contains an analytical perturbative radiation spectrum, Eq. 4, and an energy-conversion experiment in a multi-zero-dispersion fiber.
sources.where: arXiv:1506.08223; especially section 4, equation visually inspected.

sources.label: Erkintalo, Genty and Dudley (2010)
sources.note: Numerical collision-enhanced radiation peak power; the card's description as measured integrated yield is unsupported.

sources.label: Timmerkamp and Fallnich (2026)
sources.note: Integrated silicon-nitride waveguide, orthogonally polarized modes, and probe-photon conversion; not scalar-fiber pump conversion.
sources.where: Publisher-deposited Crossref abstract and Münster institution record.

sources.label: Travers et al. (2019)
sources.note: Gas-capillary source and conversion measurements; ionization and full dispersion distinguish it from the pure TOD model.
sources.where: arXiv:1811.05877; source, efficiency and limiting-regime discussion.

sources.label: Brahms, Belli and Travers (2020), PRR
sources.note: High-energy capillary compression and tunable radiation; an achievable operating point, not a ceiling.

sources.label: Brahms, Belli and Travers (2020), OL
sources.note: Pressure-gradient scaling and radiation-pulse duration; not a band-yield upper bound.

sources.label: Köttig et al. (2017)
sources.note: High repetition-rate deep-UV source using optimized gas-filled fiber stages.

sources.label: Mak et al. (2013)
sources.note: Gas-filled hollow-core tunable radiation and pressure-gradient experiments.

sources.label: Joly et al. (2011)
sources.note: Argon-filled fiber deep-UV conversion experiment; no Raman and pressure-tunable dispersion.

sources.label: Kodama and Hasegawa (1987)
sources.note: Correct bibliographic record. The specific fission-partition attribution was not checked in its full text; the baseline is reproduced in Kormokar 2023.
sources.where: Crossref publisher metadata; primary full text unavailable.

sources.label: Mollenauer et al. (1983)
sources.note: Scanned three-page reprint confirms first-compression position is measured in soliton periods, and plots compressed width and central-spike energy. The later fit constants are not independently recovered from this paper.
sources.where: Publisher abstract and bibliographically matching scanned reprint displayed at https://www.scribd.com/document/808411589/1983-L-F-Mollenauer-Extreme-picosecond-pulse-narrowing-by-means-of-soliton-effect-in-single-mode-optical-fibers; first-page theory and figure discussion read; OCR limits exact figure extraction.

sources.label: Dudley, Genty and Coen (2006)
sources.note: Broad supercontinuum review; no absence claim is inferred from its abstract.

sources.label: Skryabin et al. (2003)
sources.note: Negative dispersion slope: red Cherenkov radiation recoils the soliton toward blue and cancels Raman shift. The proposal reversed the relevant radiation direction.

sources.label: Corney and Drummond (2001), II
sources.note: Direct frequency-coordinate covariance precedes the timing-jitter formula (preprint Eq. 3.15). Analytic treatment neglects deterministic SSFS.
sources.where: arXiv:quant-ph/9912096; noise projection and sections III–IV.

sources.label: Drummond and Corney (2001), I
sources.note: The dissipative Raman susceptibility and thermal/zero-point Langevin spectrum already share a reservoir model (preprint Eqs. 6.11 and 6.16).

sources.label: Kärtner et al. (1994)
sources.note: Already models SSFS, measured Raman gain and quantum/thermal phonon noise together. The precise projected ratio is unverified without the full text.
sources.where: Optica abstract; ResearchGate publisher preview did not provide the full article.

sources.label: Haus and Lai (1990)
sources.note: Linearized quantum soliton theory includes photon-number, phase, time and frequency uncertainties.

sources.label: Gordon (1986)
sources.note: Classical fundamental-soliton self-frequency-shift law. Its energy derivative depends on how width and energy are varied.

sources.label: Santhanam and Agrawal (2003)
sources.note: General moment-method treatment and broadening-induced shift saturation; no unrestricted reach or quantum-noise floor follows from the abstract.
sources.where: ScienceDirect abstract; indexed author PDF returned 404 on direct retrieval.

sources.label: Santhanam and Agrawal (2002)
sources.note: Amplifier-noise fluctuations transferred through Raman dynamics in dispersion-managed communication systems; not the intrinsic Raman-reservoir floor.
sources.where: Indexed author-paper abstract; journal metadata checked.

sources.label: Zhou et al. (2015)
sources.note: Pump intensity noise transfers through center-wavelength changes to timing jitter; reducing accumulated dispersion reduces timing jitter.
sources.where: Publisher abstract; DESY PDF returned an empty-text page.

sources.label: Matsuo et al. (2000)
sources.note: Title, authors and DOI match. The original card's quantitative timing/intensity values were not independently checked from a primary text.
sources.where: Crossref publisher metadata; accessible primary abstract not obtained.

sources.label: Erkintalo, Genty and Dudley (2009)
sources.note: Rogue-wave-like filtered-intensity statistics; not a direct derivation of soliton centroid quantum variance.

sources.label: Kormokar and Rochette (2022)
sources.note: Conference abstract includes interpulse Raman gain in conversion efficiency. A journal version is now located.

sources.label: Kormokar, Shamim and Rochette (2023)
sources.note: Journal version, arXiv:2301.02945. Interpulse Raman transfer enhances the leading soliton beyond the Raman-independent inverse-scattering energy partition.
sources.where: arXiv full text; equations 11 and 24 and experimental comparison.

sources.label: Chen et al. (2022)
sources.note: Hydrogen hollow-core SSFS conversion; a distinct Raman reservoir from silica.

sources.label: Yi et al. (2016)
sources.note: Corrected author copy: Lagrangian shift and efficiency laws for driven cavity solitons, with large detuning and operation near the maximum existence detuning. Efficiency is relative to the minimum pump power at that operating point, not a universal conversion bound.
sources.where: Caltech author repository PDFs yi2016.pdf; derivation and stated detuning restrictions inspected.

sources.label: Yi et al. (2016), publisher’s note
sources.note: Publisher note identifies omitted text above Eq. 1 and below Eq. 15; the corrected online article is dated 19 July 2016. The corresponding operating-point assumptions were checked in the corrected author copy.
sources.where: Caltech author repository PDF yierr2016.pdf, complete one-page notice; corrected main paper read.

sources.label: Bao et al. (2021)
sources.note: Quantum timing diffusion of dissipative microcavity solitons; relevant noise precedent but a different dynamical system.

sources.label: Blow and Wood (1989)
sources.note: Correct bibliographic identity. The original wording 'energy loss by the Raman term' needs the field normalization and shock term specified; see Bonetti 2020.
sources.where: Crossref publisher metadata; primary full text not reached.

sources.label: Linale et al. (2020)
sources.note: Actual title is Measuring self-steepening with the photon-conserving nonlinear Schrödinger equation. It is an application of the model, not its founding Raman derivation.
sources.where: ITBA author manuscript; introduction and model discussion.

sources.label: Bonetti et al. (2020)
sources.note: Foundational photon-conserving generalized NLSE for frequency-dependent nonlinearities, with Raman. Standard GNLSE photon conservation requires the appropriate frequency dependence.

sources.label: Huang et al. (2026)
sources.note: The preprint exists. It derives a time-domain expansion and soliton moment equations from pcGNLSE; its conclusions cannot silently cover arbitrary lossy spectra.
sources.where: arXiv PDF/HTML; section II and moment equations.

sources.label: Gorbach and Skryabin (2007), NP
sources.note: Gravity-like radiation trapping and supercontinuum extension; supports mechanism, not a universal band-fraction ceiling.

sources.label: Gorbach and Skryabin (2007), PRA
sources.note: Section VI and Eqs. 28–30 include radiation backaction that accelerates the soliton beyond its bare Raman rate; that rate is not an upper bound.

sources.label: Skryabin and Gorbach (2010)
sources.note: Section VI reviews trapping, accelerated red shift, leakage and interactions. Blue-edge matching does not determine the blue photon fraction.

sources.label: Stone and Knight (2008)
sources.note: Uniform-fiber visible supercontinuum source; the exact group-velocity edge argument was not checked in the full text.

sources.label: Sørensen et al. (2011)
sources.note: Group-acceleration matching controls trapped blue power in tapers; group-velocity equality alone is insufficient.

sources.label: Travers (2010)
sources.note: Correct title and DOI for the blue-extension review. No mathematical claim is certified from metadata alone.
sources.where: Crossref and bibliographic record; full text not reached.

sources.label: Wetzel et al. (2018)
sources.note: Adaptive temporal pulse splitting experimentally customizes supercontinuum properties; no certified ceiling.

sources.label: Michaeli and Bahabad (2018)
sources.note: Genetic-algorithm control of shaped supercontinuum spectra.

sources.label: Hary et al. (2023)
sources.note: Genetic optimization of narrow spectral channels; enhancement relative to a reference is not absolute conversion efficiency.

sources.label: Hary et al. (2025)
sources.note: Comparison of genetic, particle-swarm and annealing optimization. GPT independently read the abstract; the retained Claude proposal reports full-text access.
sources.where: Publisher-deposited Crossref abstract; Nature full-page retrieval failed.

sources.label: Lee et al. (2023)
sources.note: Free-form SiN waveguides optimized for power, flatness and coherence using particle-swarm optimization; this cited work is not an adjoint-gradient method.
sources.where: arXiv PDF; design method and objectives.

sources.label: Shamim, Alamgir and Rochette (2023)
sources.note: The source of the quoted high-efficiency tuning range. Distinct from the Kormokar fission-efficiency journal paper; pulse compression preserves soliton order.
sources.where: Optica journal abstract and McGill author-copy abstract.

sources.label: Kormokar, Shamim and Rochette (2021)
sources.note: Adiabatic, nearly unchirped fundamental-soliton drift including TOD, shock and loss; Sections 2.3–3 derive the reduced law. Section 4.2.2 notes that the ansatz omits dispersive radiation. Not an all-field reach bound or a noise theory.
sources.where: Author preprint mirrored at https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/e7f5/ff2b482f21657c3860c55fb42e0c94d43cae.pdf; local kormokar2021.pdf; Sections 2.3–3 and 4.2.2 inspected.

sources.label: Yang et al. (2021)
sources.note: Cavity quiet-point noise suppression balances Raman shift and dispersive-wave recoil, with added thermal noise. Relevant precedent for including the dynamical noise transfer.

sources.label: Tsang (2007)
sources.note: Pulse position/frequency operators, optical-loss noise and adiabatic quantum soliton control. Raman is explicitly outside the analyzed model; this does not settle an SSFS noise floor.
sources.where: NUS author PDF https://www.ece.nus.edu.sg/stfpage/tmk/papers/tsang_decoherence_quantum-enhanced_timing_accuracy_PRA.pdf via indexed full text; Sections II and IV.D/VI inspected.

sources.label: Zheltikov (2018), SPM theory
sources.note: Approximate short-distance SPM/GVD broadening and high-order compression-length scaling. Section 3 Eq. 6 includes the soliton-period factor omitted from the proposal’s leading compression-length coefficient.
sources.where: Publisher full article mirrored on ResearchGate https://www.researchgate.net/publication/325913147_Analytical_insights_into_self-phase_modulation_beyond_the_basic_theory; Sections 3–4, Eqs. 6 and 11–14 inspected.
